correctness.rationale: With \(f(t)=t/(1+t)\), strict monotonicity gives the pointwise identity \(\min\{f(a),f(b)\}=f(\min\{a,b\})\). Continuity and monotonicity give \(\sup f(m)=f(\sup m)\) even without attainment, proving the transform exactly. For the printed corollary, the source's bound \(J_1\le2/3\) makes its right-hand side negative, while the modulus of smoothness at one is nonnegative. No finite experiment is needed.

value.rationale: The proof is short, but the conclusion is structurally consequential rather than a cosmetic substitution: it collapses a published geometric invariant to an invertible transform of a classical one, transfers all numerical thresholds automatically, and exposes a concrete impossible corollary in the defining source.
residual_risks: Because the identity is elementary, it may have appeared in an unindexed note or informal correction.

final_claim: For every real Banach space of dimension at least two, the metric James-type constant \(J_1(X)\) introduced in 2022 satisfies exactly \(J_1(X)=J(X)/(1+J(X))\), so it carries no numerical information beyond the classical James constant; the same source's printed Corollary 2 is impossible as written.
limitations: The finding does not propose an optimal replacement for the erroneous modulus-of-smoothness corollary.
It does not audit the source's other three James-type constants.
